ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, and beneficial owners against FINTRAC guidance, Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and the OFAC SDN list as a best-practice cross-border standard. Positive matches are escalated to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer; a hit requires enhanced due diligence, potential refusal of service, and reporting to FINTRAC where applicable under Canadian law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services - BC Corporate Online via https://bcregistry.ca/corporates; NUANS name search through Corporations Canada-accredited search agency
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, a BC company name may be in English, French, or a combination. If the proposed corporate name contains characters from a foreign script, the registry requires a transliteration or romanized rendering, a certified English or French phonetic equivalent, and, where used as a corporate name, a registered English or French-language legal element. The statutory prohibition applies to confusingly similar, prohibited, or names contrary to the public interest. All filings in BC Corporate Online are completed in English; a non-English devised name requires prior transliteration review.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may receive a formal rejection notice with the reason code. Within 30 days, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration or an amended name reservation using BC Corporate Online, paying the applicable reconsideration or name-reservation fee. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may submit a formal administrative review request to the Registrar of Companies and thereafter apply for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, within the applicable limitation period. Where the rejection is based on trademark or confusing similarity, the applicant may provide a consent letter from the prior rights holder or disclaim the conflicting element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only for the statutory registered office address when using a licensed BC corporate agent or registered office service under the Business Corporations Act; virtual office does not satisfy the physical premises, municipal business licence, or public-health requirements for a specialty tea salon or lounge. The operating trading address must be an actual commercial location in British Columbia, subject to municipal zoning and food-service inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 70-90% probability of an unannounced municipal public-health or food-service inspection within the first 12 months of operation; any food-service or zoning anomaly increases follow-up inspection frequency. Corporate books and records inspection is unlikely absent a tax audit, regulatory suspicion, or complaint, estimated at under 15% annual base probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c. 57), ss. 10 (incorporation application), 11 (notice of articles), 12 (articles), 22 (registered office), 24 (directors), and 51 (share capital).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, Corporate Online, Ministry of Finance
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) together with Articles
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Authorized share structure and classes are set in the Notice of Articles; no escrow or minimum capitalization requirement imposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation application dated [date] and the Notice of Articles and Articles submitted to the BC Registrar of Companies be approved and ratified; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the initial share subscription be accepted and shares issued to the subscribers as set out in the Notice of Articles; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at [registered office address], British Columbia; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the persons named as directors in the Notice of Articles are appointed as the first directors, and the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer; RESOLVED FURTHER, that management is authorized to open bank accounts and to make all filings and applications necessary to begin specialty tea salon operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies – Corporate Online (www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request or NUANS search, select a distinct legal name for use in British Columbia, pay the name reservation fee, and secure the approved name before filing the incorporation application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, request anew name review with supporting distinguishing words or numerals; appeal through the BC Registry name review process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Notice of Articles and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies – Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Notice of Articles and Articles in compliance with the BC Business Corporations Act, including share classes, number of shares, first directors, registered office address, and corporate objects. Ensure all required signatures are obtained.
required_dossiers: Director Address and Birth Date Information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formatting or statutory omissions and re-submit the amended documents via Corporate Online; the Registry will issue a deficiency notice identifying required changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application and Pay Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies – Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Notice of Articles and Articles through Corporate Online, pay the filing fee, and receive the electronic acknowledgement and transaction number confirming the incorporation application is accepted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, review the Registry deficiency letter, correct the identified errors, and refile; the filing fee may be forfeited if the initial filing is invalid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / Canada Revenue Agency via OneStop Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the formal Certificate of Incorporation from Corporate Online and activate the federal/provincial Business Number through the Canada Revenue Agency, including GST/PST registration and payroll account opening if applicable.
required_dossiers: CRA Account Application (RC201 style form if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact the CRA Business Registration line to reconcile the Business Number and update corporate accounts; resubmit missing tax elections to avoid retroactive penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve Initial Directors and Officers by Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies – Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the written resolutions approving share issuance, registered office, and officer appointments, and file any required director or officer change notices with the BC Registrar.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director or Officer
Notice of Directors (if different from Notice of Articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the change notice, verify the effective date and officer residential addresses; file a corrected Notice at the earliest opportunity to avoid late-filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Municipal Business Licence and Health Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licence Office and Vancouver Coastal Health Environmental Health
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Business Licence application for a specialty tea salon, attach the premises floor plan and zoning approval, and apply for a food establishment permit with Vancouver Coastal Health before commencing operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit revised fire safety and sanitation plans if inspection fails; request a compliance meeting with municipal inspectors and re-inspection after corrective actions are completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Provincial Tax and Workers Compensation Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC OneStop Business Registry and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the BC OneStop registration for provincial sales tax and employer obligations, and register with WorkSafeBC for occupational injury coverage if any staff are employed; obtain the WorkSafeBC clearance certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If automated registration fails, contact OneStop Business Registry for manual enrolment and file directly with the BC Ministry of Finance, then complete WorkSafeBC registration separately.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – not a reviewable project under the BC Environmental Assessment Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to municipal sewer per municipal sewer bylaw; grease interceptor required if food preparation creates grease; no meaningful VOC emissions; solid waste handling must comply with BC Environmental Management Act and municipal waste bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification under BC Fire Code; structural load and building occupancy review under BC Building Code; electrical and plumbing permits; WorkplaceBC occupational health and safety clearance for staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Agence du revenu du Canada, federal tax administration for GST/HST and corporate income tax, accessed via the CRA My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Provincial sales tax in British Columbia is administered separately by the BC Ministry of Finance via the eTaxBC PST portal (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/sales-taxes/pst).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canada uses the nine-digit Business Number (BN) as the statutory tax identifier. A Canadian business corporation obtains its BN and GST/HST registration concurrently either online through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or by filing Form RC1/RC1CO (Request for Business Number and Certain Accounts). Registration must be applied for within 30 days after the small-supplier threshold is exceeded (ETA s.242(1)). The CRA issues the BN plus program accounts: RC for corporate income tax and RT for GST/HST; RP payroll and RM import/export program accounts may be added at filing. A foreign-owned Canadian corporation may complete the application electronically without a fiscal representative, but CRA reserves the power under ETA s.241 to require a non-resident registrant to post security or appoint an agent on collection-risk grounds. BC PST vendor registration is a separate filing through the BC eTaxBC portal using the same BN and is required once the corporation begins selling taxable goods or services in British Columbia.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; a Business Corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the British Columbia Business Corporations Act is mandatorily taxed as an entity at the corporate level. Available elections include: (a) the GST/HST closely-related corporation election under ETA s.156, which treats taxable supplies between associated registrants as made for nil consideration and can be applied to inter-company tea-stock transfers, royalties, and management services; (b) the functional currency election under ITA s.261 for an eligible Canadian corporation reporting in a prescribed foreign currency; (c) corporate reorganization rollover elections under ITA s.85 for transfer of business assets to a related corporation; and (d) the GST/HST Quick Method accounting election under ETA s.227.1 for small registrants with annual taxable supplies not exceeding C$400,000. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss.18.4(3)-(5) are self-executing disallowance/recharacterization provisions with no elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a federal value-added tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; British Columbia does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) and instead imposes a separate 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST), producing a combined BC consumption levy of 12% on taxable retail supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 - GST/HST small-supplier threshold under ETA s.240(1). Registration is mandatory once the person's worldwide taxable supplies, including those of associated persons, exceed C$30,000 in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or, once exceeded in the current calendar quarter, thereafter until the threshold is no longer exceeded. Zero-rated export supplies count as taxable supplies for the threshold; exempt supplies do not. For BC PST there is no general monetary small-supplier threshold: registration is required upon commencing a taxable business of selling goods or providing taxable services in British Columbia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no government pre-stamping, and no API-based clearance obligation for GST/HST invoices. A registrant must issue a GST/HST invoice containing the vendor's Business Number, invoice date, date of supply, total consideration, and GST/HST charged, and must retain full source documentation. Electronic invoicing, including PEPPOL-standard e-invoices, is legally valid and accepted by CRA where records are complete, legible, and accessible to audit. The Government of Canada has adopted PEPPOL for federal procurement digitization, but no B2B e-invoicing mandate applies to a specialty tea salon. The BC PST regime similarly requires itemized PST disclosure on invoices and retention of sales and export records, with no fiscal clearance or digital stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a supply of tangible personal property, such as packaged ceremonial teas, loose-leaf blends, tea ware, and ceramics, is zero-rated under ETA s.19(1) where the property is exported by the supplier or the non-resident recipient as part of the supply, ordinarily within 60 days of delivery to an international carrier, and the supplier retains the prescribed customs and shipping evidence. Services: a supply of services, including online tea-culture education, custom blend consulting, and cultural salon programming, is zero-rated under ETA s.22(1) where the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST, the service is not rendered to an individual present in Canada, and the service does not relate to real property in Canada or to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance; the place-of-supply rules of ETA ss.18.1-18.2 must direct the supply outside Canada. A registrant making predominantly zero-rated exports may claim full input tax credits for GST paid on inputs, including imported tea leaf, kilns, and lease costs, and may recover excess ITCs refundable in the ordinary net GST return. In-store retail tea service at the BC salon remains taxable at 5% GST plus 7% PST and is never zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) electronic export declaration (B13A / legacy G13 equivalent)
Commercial invoice with HS tariff codes, quantity, unit values, and country of destination
Bill of Lading / Through Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill / Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Canada
Packing list and freight or courier receipt confirming handover to an international carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / bank credit advice evidencing repatriation of export proceeds to Canada
Signed non-resident declaration and GST/HST non-registration confirmation from the foreign purchaser for zero-rated services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and the Canada Border Services Agency jointly verify export zero-rating claims through documentary audits, carrier record matching, and cross-border data analytics. Failure to maintain the prescribed documentation bundle causes reversal of the zero-rating and assessment of uncollected GST at 5% (plus BC PST where applicable) for the entire review period, with statutory interest from the original due dates. The normal four-year reassessment limit is extended without limitation where the registrant has made a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or willful default (ETA s.298(3)). Civil penalties for false statements or omissions in returns and rebate applications under ETA s.280(1) et seq. start at C$100 and may reach 50% of the tax shortfall or rebate overclaimed; repeated or systemic diversion of export documentation can trigger aggregated penalties. Wilful evasion or fraudulent suppression of export records is prosecutable under Criminal Code s.380 as fraud, carrying imprisonment of up to 14 years. Independently, CBSA Administrative Monetary Penalty System (AMPS) penalties apply to inaccurate or non-compliant export declarations, up to C$5,000 per violation, and CRA may require security or block further zero-rated treatment pending audit cooperation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (annual corporate return filed online under the Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registry, Corporate Online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year within 2 months after the company's incorporation anniversary; annual report may be submitted from 1 month before the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late-filing penalty; continued default may trigger a notice of intention to strike-off and eventual administrative dissolution by the Registrar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and annual resolutions/minutes (director and shareholder resolutions recorded in the minute book; no separate registry filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the registered office (not filed with the Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held no later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end; minutes and register updates recorded immediately after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct Registry financial penalty; failure to hold an AGM may risk loss of director limitation protection, court-ordered meeting remedies, and shareholder enforcement action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (T2), including British Columbia provincial corporate tax administered through the federal filing process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); BC provincial corporate tax is integrated in the T2 return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the taxation year-end; balance-due date is generally within 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs and 3 months for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat failure may add a 10% penalty; daily compound interest applies to unpaid balances

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST return for annual filers (required for specialty tea lounge and prepared beverage sales if taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 registration threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers must file within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; quarterly or monthly filers must file and remit by the prescribed period-end date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 6% or 10% for failure to file, plus daily interest on unremitted GST/HST; gross negligence penalties may apply for repeated or deliberate omissions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent auditor is mandatory for BC reporting issuers, public companies, and distributing corporations. Private companies may waive the auditor appointment for a fiscal year only with shareholder consent; the waiver cannot be used if any shareholder objects or an external regulator, lender, or the articles require an audit. There is no general revenue-based audit threshold under the BC Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook) is required for reporting issuers and publicly accountable enterprises; private enterprises may apply ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook). The T2 corporate return and GST/HST filing schedules must follow the chosen accounting basis consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate annual UBO filing to the BC Registry. BC companies must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) transparency register at the registered office, update it within 15 days of knowledge of any change, and perform a documented annual internal confirmation that share transfers and ISC changes are reflected accurately. Any transfer that alters significant control must be recorded in the applicable corporate registers and minute book.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: Federal rate reduced to 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; BC rate reduced to 2% on same threshold. Additional incentives: Investment Tax Credits for SR&ED, etc.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed via CRA e-file (NETFILE for corporations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly tax installments required if tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income (all sources, including business income, interest, dividends)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source income; attach Form T2046 if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions (business expenses, capital cost allowance, etc.)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses reasonably allocable to Canadian-source income
Apply treaty provisions to reduce taxable income if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax (calculated at 15% general rate or 9% small business rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use federal rate applicable to non-resident corporations with permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax (BC rate 12% general or 2% small business)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: BC tax applies only if permanent establishment in BC; otherwise allocate income to other provinces

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable (sum of federal and provincial tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all credits and treaty relief are claimed before final payment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rates; additional penalties for repeated failures

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) to the Canadian payer; payer completes Form NR301 (or NR302 for treaty-based withholding) and submits to CRA. For Canada-US, rate reduced to 15% (or 5% if 10%+ ownership).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty often 10% (e.g., US, UK). Interest: statutory 25%, treaty often 0% (e.g., US) or 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000 (goods) or CAD 500,000 (services) or CAD 250,000 (interest). Master File required if group revenue exceeds CAD 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a standalone ESR. However, CRA applies general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions; substance is required to claim treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful understatement of income, false deductions, or failure to file returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to 50% of tax evaded; criminal prosecution with fines up to 200% of tax and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they failed to withhold or remit; travel bans and asset seizure possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificial transactions, no real business activity, or treaty shopping without substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, penalties for negligence, and potential criminal charges
